summary.title: Practical SQL for Data Analysis
summary.one_liner: Learn how doing aggregation, sampling, random data generation and train/test splits inside PostgreSQL can cut memory use and runtime compared with pandas.
takeaways: Aggregating in PostgreSQL and fetching only the results uses far less memory and time than loading a full table into pandas (347 MB and 1.101s down to 2.3 MB and 0.114s in the author's benchmark).
Use generate_series, VALUES, UNNEST and random() with ceil (not round) to generate test data and uniform random integers.
TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM is much faster than ORDER BY random() for sampling large tables, at the cost of some accuracy; BERNOULLI is a row-level compromise.
A train/test split can be done in SQL with CREATE TABLE ... AS TABLE ... WITH NO DATA and a WITH ... INSERT ... RETURNING CTE.
Pandas and SQL work best together: push heavy aggregation to the database and use pandas for the rest.
summary.summary: The article argues that many data analysis tasks can be done inside a SQL database rather than by loading everything into pandas. The author benchmarks a counting task on a 1M-row PostgreSQL table using memory-profiler and psycopg2, comparing pandas variants against aggregation in the database and a plain Python version. It then covers SQL basics for analysis: CTEs, generating data (UNION ALL, VALUES, UNNEST, generate_series), random number and sampling techniques, a train/test split example, and descriptive statistics such as percentile_cont. The page ends mid-explanation of ordered-set aggregate functions.
